diagnosis.summary: Flink job `events-to-iceberg` suffered ~2 checkpoint failures ~2 minutes ago when its taskmanager pod was killed (chaos-mesh experiment); the job has since auto-restarted, is RUNNING/STABLE, and is completing ~25 checkpoints per 5 minutes again. No action needed — the platform is recovering on its own.
diagnosis.root_cause: A chaos-mesh experiment (chaos-mesh-local deployed ~27 min ago, with an earlier round ~144 min ago that also killed all Kafka brokers) killed the Flink taskmanager pod ~1.9 minutes before the investigation. The abrupt TaskExecutor shutdown aborted an in-flight checkpoint, generating the ~2 failures that triggered the alert. The Flink operator automatically restarted the job from its latest checkpoint; it has been RUNNING/STABLE for ~96 seconds with successful checkpoints resuming immediately (25 completed in the last 5 minutes at the expected ~10 s cadence). Consumer lag of 650 is a backlog from the downtime and will drain normally.
diagnosis.impact: Approximately 2 checkpoints failed, causing a brief (<2 min) gap in exactly-once guarantees and a consumer lag backlog of ~650 messages. No data loss is expected as Flink recovered from its last good checkpoint. Iceberg data visibility was delayed by at most one job-restart window.

evidence.finding: Job RUNNING, lifecycle STABLE; uptime_seconds=96 (just restarted); restarts_last_15m=1.018; failed_checkpoints_last_10m=2.104; completed_checkpoints_last_5m=24.995; consumer_lag=650. Taskmanager pod events-to-iceberg-taskmanager-2-2 is only 1.9 minutes old.

Warning JobException on FlinkDeployment/events-to-iceberg 1.9 min ago: 'org.apache.flink.util.FlinkExpectedException: The TaskExecutor is shutting down' — confirms abrupt taskmanager termination caused the checkpoint failure.

chaos-mesh-local deployed at 144.6 min ago (revision 9187ff9e9e6f) and again at 27.0 min ago (revision 47886843e767); platform-local also synced at 28.7 min ago. Chaos experiments timed with all pod terminations.

All 3 Kafka brokers Running/Ready; under_replicated_partitions=0, under_min_isr_partitions=0, offline_partitions=0. All brokers show last_termination ~140.9 min ago (exit_code 255, reason Unknown) — consistent with an earlier chaos experiment, now fully recovered.
All 4 nodes Ready (control-plane + 3 workers across zone-a/b/c), no pressure conditions, none unschedulable. Node layer is healthy.
Only FlinkCheckpointFailures and OpsAgentInvestigationsFailing are firing; no Kafka, node, or replication alerts active.

docs/runbooks/pipeline.md#flinkcheckpointfailures states: 'A single failure during a broker restart or node drain is expected'; job tolerates 3 consecutive failures before restarting — fits the observed 2 failures during taskmanager churn.

proposed_action.rationale: The job is already RUNNING and STABLE with 25 successful checkpoints in the last 5 minutes. The failure was caused by a chaos-mesh-induced taskmanager kill and was self-healing via the Flink operator restart. Restarting the job or any pod now would interrupt the recovery already in progress and would not address the root cause (chaos experiments).

follow_ups: Monitor alert clearance: failed_checkpoints_last_10m should drop to 0 within the next 10 minutes as the failure window slides out; if it does not, re-investigate.
Consumer lag of 650 should drain within minutes at normal throughput; set a lag alert threshold to catch if it stalls.

Confirm the chaos-mesh experiment that killed the taskmanager ~2 min ago was intentional and scheduled — the timing of chaos-mesh-local deployments at 144, 94, 44, and 27 minutes ago suggests active chaos testing; ensure experiments are scoped away from production hours if applicable.

The earlier chaos round ~140.9 min ago terminated all 3 Kafka brokers simultaneously (exit_code 255) which is more severe than a single-broker loss; verify min.insync.replicas was not violated during that event by checking Kafka under-min-ISR metrics for that window.
OpsAgentInvestigationsFailing alert is also firing — investigate the ops-agent's own health separately.
